title: Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce: 2026 Comparison for APAC
summary: A Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 comparison built for APAC merchants: real TCO including headcount, release cadence, regional payments and a decision framework.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** For most APAC retail merchants under 100,000 SKUs with more merchandisers than engineers, Shopify Plus delivers better outcomes despite a higher licence. Adobe Commerce wins for true quote-to-cash B2B, dealer hierarchies, complex catalogues, or existing Adobe estates — provided you can retain engineering capacity.


---


Most Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 comparison articles argue about licence fees. That is the least interesting number in the decision. I have sat in enough replatform steering committees across Hong Kong, Singapore, Taipei and Kuala Lumpur to say it plainly: the platform licence is rarely what kills a project. What kills it is the headcount you did not budget for, the local payment method that needed a custom module, and the twelve months your merchandising team spent waiting on a release train.


*Related reading:*[Shopify Plus Enterprise Fit & Cost Comparison for APAC Brands](https://branch8.com/posts/shopify-plus-enterprise-fit-cost-comparison-apac)


*Related reading:*[Agentic Commerce Protocol ChatGPT Checkout: APAC Build Guide](https://branch8.com/posts/agentic-commerce-protocol-chatgpt-checkout-apac-guide)


So this comparison is built differently. Instead of a feature grid, I am going to look at three things that actually determine outcomes for Asia-Pacific merchants: total cost of ownership including people, operational efficiency measured in release cadence, and regional feature parity across payments, logistics and language. Then I will give you a decision framework you can run in two weeks.


## The verdict, up front


If your business is retail-led, sells in three to eight markets, runs a catalogue under roughly 100,000 SKUs, and your merchandising team outnumbers your engineering team, Shopify Plus will almost certainly produce better commercial outcomes in 2026. Not because it is technically superior — in several dimensions it is not — but because it removes the operations layer that APAC mid-market teams are least equipped to staff.


*Related reading:*[Salesforce CRM OAuth Security Incident Response: APAC Playbook](https://branch8.com/posts/salesforce-crm-oauth-security-incident-response-apac-playbook)


*Related reading:*[Salesforce OAuth Token Security Breach Mitigation for APAC Teams](https://branch8.com/posts/salesforce-oauth-token-security-breach-mitigation-apac)


If you run genuinely complex B2B (customer-specific pricing matrices, multi-tier dealer hierarchies, quote-to-order workflows), you have an existing Adobe Experience Cloud estate, or your catalogue and pricing logic resist productisation, Adobe Commerce remains the stronger foundation — provided you accept that you are buying a development platform, not a product, and you staff accordingly.


*Related reading:*[B2B Ecommerce Development Partner Selection: A Buyer's Guide](https://branch8.com/posts/b2b-ecommerce-development-partner-selection)


The honest middle ground: for the majority of APAC merchants doing between USD 5M and USD 100M in online GMV, the Adobe Commerce cost advantage that appears in a three-year licence comparison tends to be consumed by engineering and DevOps cost. Agency analyses in this space, including[IWD Agency's 2026 breakdown](https://www.iwdagency.com/) , put a Shopify Plus three-year total near USD 540K against roughly USD 350K for Adobe Commerce on raw direct cost — then note the operational complexity Adobe adds. That gap is real, and it is narrower than it looks once you price the team.


## Why the APAC decision diverges from the US one


North American comparisons assume Stripe or Braintree, UPS or FedEx, and English-only storefronts. None of that holds here.


A Hong Kong merchant needs FPS, AlipayHK, WeChat Pay HK and Octopus. Singapore needs PayNow and GrabPay. Taiwan needs convenience-store pickup and payment at FamilyMart and 7-Eleven, plus ECPay or NewebPay as the gateway, plus government-mandated e-invoicing. Malaysia and Indonesia need FPX, GrabPay, ShopeePay and bank transfer with manual reconciliation. Australia and New Zealand need Afterpay and Zip. Japan needs konbini and Amazon Pay.


According to[Worldpay's Global Payments Report](https://worldpay.globalpaymentsreport.com/) , digital wallets account for the majority of Asia-Pacific e-commerce transaction value — a far higher share than in Europe or North America. This is the single biggest driver of hidden cost in an APAC replatform, and it is where the two platforms behave very differently.


Shopify Plus covers the major APAC wallets through Shopify Payments in supported markets and through a long tail of certified gateway apps elsewhere. Coverage is good but not complete, and where it is missing you are waiting on a partner, not writing code — Shopify restricts custom payment gateway development to approved providers. Adobe Commerce lets you build anything, which means you can always solve the problem, and you will always pay to solve it. For Taiwan convenience-store logistics in particular, I have seen both paths taken: a marketplace extension on Adobe that needs upgrading every minor release, versus a Shopify app with a narrower feature set that someone else maintains.


That trade-off — write it yourself forever, or accept someone else's scope — is the real Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce decision in this region.

## Total cost of ownership: the four lines that matter


### Platform licence


Shopify publishes its enterprise pricing openly: Plus starts at[USD 2,300 per month on a three-year term](https://www.shopify.com/plus) , rising to USD 2,500 on a one-year term, with variable pricing above roughly USD 800K monthly GMV. Predictable, boring, easy to model.


Adobe does not publish Adobe Commerce pricing. Third-party estimates circulating in 2026 comparisons put Adobe Commerce on Cloud between USD 22,000 and USD 125,000 per year depending on GMV band and order volume, with the figure scaling against average order value and catalogue size. Adobe's own[product pages](https://business.adobe.com/products/magento/magento-commerce.html) confirm the licence is quoted, not listed. Treat any specific number you read online as an estimate, including the ones above.


### Implementation


This is where the ratio is most consistent in my experience across Greater China and Southeast Asia. An Adobe Commerce enterprise build typically runs two to three times the implementation cost of an equivalent Shopify Plus build, because you are constructing more of the system yourself: theme layer, admin extensions, integration middleware, deployment pipeline, test coverage.


Shopify Plus builds compress because the checkout, the admin, the multi-store architecture and the hosting are given. You spend your budget on storefront experience, ERP integration and merchandising tooling instead of foundations.


### Running cost — the line most shortlists underprice


Adobe Commerce needs people. A realistic steady-state team for a mid-market APAC merchant is one to two backend developers who know Magento's dependency injection and plugin system, a frontend developer, and meaningful DevOps capacity for the Cloud pipeline. In Hong Kong and Singapore, senior Magento engineers are scarce and expensive; in Vietnam and the Philippines they are available and competitively priced, which is exactly why offshore and nearshore delivery models matter so much to this decision. A global brand running Adobe Commerce with an APAC engineering base in Ho Chi Minh City or Manila has a genuinely different cost structure from one staffing in Sydney.


Shopify Plus running cost shifts into app subscriptions — and these add up faster than finance teams expect. Subscription billing, advanced search, product reviews, loyalty, B2B pricing logic, ERP connectors: a Plus merchant commonly carries USD 1,500 to USD 5,000 per month in app spend. That is a real cost, but it is OPEX with a vendor on the hook for maintenance, not headcount you must retain.


### Upgrade and security burden


Adobe ships security patches and version upgrades on a published cadence documented in the[Adobe Commerce release notes](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/release/notes/overview) . Each one is a project: regression test, fix broken extensions, redeploy. Merchants that skip them accumulate risk — Magento has historically been a popular target for card-skimming attacks precisely because so many instances run unpatched. Shopify Plus upgrades happen underneath you. You do not get a choice, which is both the benefit and the constraint.


## Operational efficiency: measure release cadence, not features


The metric I push every client to examine before signing anything: how many days from "marketing wants a new landing page template with a custom promotion rule" to live in production?


On Shopify Plus with a well-built Online Store 2.0 theme or a Hydrogen storefront, a merchandiser does most of this alone through sections and metafields. Promotion logic lands in Shopify Functions, which run server-side at checkout without a developer in the loop at campaign time.


A discount function skeleton in JavaScript looks like this:


```text
1  // extensions/volume-discount/src/run.js     2   export     function     run  (  input  )     {     3      const   targets   =   input  .  cart  .  lines     4        .  filter  (  (  line  )     =>   line  .  quantity     >=     10  )     5        .  map  (  (  line  )     =>     (  {     cartLine  :     {     id  :   line  .  id     }     }  )  )  ;     6
7      if     (  targets  .  length     ===     0  )     return     {     discounts  :     [  ]     }  ;     8
9      return     {     10        discountApplicationStrategy  :     "MAXIMUM"  ,     11        discounts  :     [  {     12        targets  ,     13          value  :     {     percentage  :     {     value  :     "12.0"     }     }  ,     14          message  :     "Bulk order discount"     15        }  ]     16      }  ;     17   }
```


Deploy with` shopify app deploy` , and the rule is live. No release train, no regression suite across a monolith. The[Shopify developer documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api) covers Functions, Checkout UI extensions and the Admin GraphQL API in detail.


The Adobe equivalent is a module. You write a plugin or an observer, register it in` di.xml` , add tests, and ship through the deployment pipeline:


```text
1  bin/magento module:enable Vendor_VolumeDiscount    2  bin/magento setup:upgrade    3  bin/magento setup:di:compile    4  bin/magento cache:flush
```


That is more powerful — you can express pricing logic Shopify Functions simply cannot reach, including rules that depend on external ERP state at request time. It is also a software release every time. For a merchant running 40 campaigns a year across six markets, the cumulative drag is substantial.


The honest counterpoint: Shopify's checkout extensibility model is deliberately bounded. If your business requires checkout behaviour outside what Checkout UI extensions and Functions permit — unusual tax treatment, a bespoke multi-party split payment, a region-specific invoicing flow — you will hit a wall you cannot code around. Adobe has no such wall. Know which side of that line your requirements sit on before you choose.

## Regional feature parity: where each platform concedes ground


**Multi-market and multi-currency.** Shopify Markets handles market-specific domains, pricing, duties and local payment methods from one admin, documented in[Shopify's Markets help centre](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/markets) . For a brand running Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore and Australia, this is considerably less work than Adobe's store-view and website hierarchy, which gives you finer control at the cost of configuration sprawl. I have seen Adobe estates with sixteen store views where nobody on the team could reliably say which configuration scope a given value was inheriting from.


**Language.** Both handle Traditional and Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai and Bahasa. Adobe's translation is file-based and developer-mediated; Shopify's is admin-editable and app-assisted. Advantage Shopify for teams without engineers, advantage Adobe for teams with strict terminology governance.


**Tax and compliance.** This is Adobe's quiet strength in APAC. Taiwan's e-invoice (電子發票) requirements, Indonesia's e-Faktur, India's GST filings — these often need platform-level customisation. Shopify merchants typically solve them with a regional app or a middleware layer. Both work; Adobe gives you more direct control.


**Logistics.** Shopify's APAC carrier app coverage has improved materially — SF Express, J&T, Ninja Van, Australia Post, convenience-store pickup in Taiwan. Adobe's shipping extension landscape is deeper but more fragmented in quality.


## B2B and dealer networks: Adobe's clearest win


If you sell through a dealer, distributor or franchise network, read this section twice.


Adobe Commerce B2B — company accounts, hierarchical buyer roles, requisition lists, negotiable quotes, shared catalogues with per-company pricing — is included and mature, per[Adobe's B2B documentation](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-admin/b2b/introduction) . Shopify's B2B on Plus has closed much of the gap since 2023 with company profiles, price lists, payment terms and draft orders, but it remains shallower on quote negotiation workflows and deep account hierarchies.


We have worked with manufacturers selling through dealer networks across Greater China where the pricing model alone — tier, volume, contract, territory and promotional overlays resolved per line item against ERP state — determined the platform. When pricing logic cannot be expressed as a price list, Adobe is the answer. When it can, Shopify B2B plus a pricing app is usually faster and cheaper to run.


The nuance most comparison reports miss: a lot of "B2B" in APAC is actually wholesale ordering with negotiated price lists, not true quote-to-cash. That subset fits Shopify B2B well. Be precise about which you have.

## Performance: Shopify's structural advantage


Shopify Plus serves from a globally distributed infrastructure with checkout and CDN handled for you. Adobe Commerce performance is a function of how well your build and hosting were engineered — Fastly caching, Redis configuration, indexer strategy, Elasticsearch or OpenSearch tuning. A well-engineered Adobe site is fast. A typical one is not.


This matters commercially.[Google's web.dev guidance on Core Web Vitals](https://web.dev/vitals/) documents the conversion relationship, and in APAC it is amplified by mobile share — mobile accounts for the majority of e-commerce sessions across Southeast Asia, higher than the global average. On 4G in Jakarta or Manila, a two-second difference in Largest Contentful Paint is not a vanity metric.


Adobe's SaaS-delivered Commerce editions and Edge Delivery Services are narrowing this gap, and that is the most consequential Adobe development heading into 2026. If you are evaluating Adobe now, evaluate the SaaS path, not the 2019 self-managed picture.


## When to choose Shopify Plus


- Your merchandising and marketing headcount exceeds your engineering headcount, and you want it to stay that way.
- You operate three to eight markets and want market-level pricing and payments without a store-view matrix.
- Catalogue is under roughly 100,000 SKUs with conventional pricing logic.
- You need to launch in six months, not eighteen.
- Your B2B need is wholesale ordering with price lists, not negotiated quote-to-cash.
- You are a US, UK or EU brand entering Asia and want to pilot three markets before committing engineering capital. This is the strongest Shopify case there is.
- You would rather pay a predictable licence plus app fees than carry retained specialist engineers.

## When to choose Adobe Commerce


- Dealer, distributor or franchise networks with hierarchical accounts and genuine quote workflows.
- Catalogue complexity that defeats productisation — configurable product trees, bundle logic, attribute-driven pricing at scale.
- An existing Adobe Experience Manager or Analytics estate where shared data and content tooling create real leverage.
- Regulatory or invoicing requirements in Taiwan, Indonesia or India that need platform-level control.
- You already have, or can reliably staff, an engineering team — including via a delivery base in Vietnam, the Philippines or Malaysia where Magento talent is available at sustainable cost.
- Checkout behaviour that Shopify's extensibility model will not permit. Verify this specifically; do not assume it.


## The option most APAC shortlists skip


If your business is concentrated in Greater China or Southeast Asia and heavily social-commerce-driven, SHOPLINE deserves a slot on the shortlist. Native integration with WhatsApp, LINE, Facebook and Instagram commerce, regional payment coverage out of the box, and local-language support are genuinely stronger than either global platform for merchants whose primary channel is conversational. It is weaker on international expansion and on developer extensibility. For a Hong Kong or Taiwan retailer selling domestically through social, running the three-way comparison rather than the two-way one is the more honest exercise.

## A two-week decision framework


Run these five steps in order. Stop when one produces a decisive answer.


**1. Write down your non-negotiable requirements.** Not features — requirements. "Per-dealer contract pricing resolved against SAP at cart time" is a requirement. "Good B2B" is not. If any non-negotiable fails Shopify's extensibility boundaries, the decision is made.


**2. Count your team, honestly.** How many engineers can you retain for three years? Not hire once — retain. If the answer is fewer than two who can own a Magento codebase, Adobe self-managed is off the table regardless of licence cost.


**3. Map your payment and logistics matrix per market.** List every payment method and carrier you need in every market. Check coverage on both platforms. Price the gaps. This usually reshapes the cost model more than the licence does.


**4. Model five-year TCO including people.** Licence, implementation, apps or extensions, retained engineering, DevOps, upgrade projects, and the cost of delay on campaigns you could not ship. Build the comparison chart yourself; do not inherit one from a vendor.


**5. Run one real scenario end to end.** Take your most awkward promotion or pricing rule and have each shortlisted partner show you how it is built, deployed and changed six months later. The answer to "how do we change this later" tells you more than any demo.


## Who this advice is not for


If you are doing over USD 500M in online GMV with a dedicated platform engineering organisation, ignore most of the operational-efficiency argument above — at that scale you can absorb complexity, and the composable or Adobe path may well give you leverage Shopify's boundaries cannot. If you are under USD 2M GMV, neither platform is your answer; Shopify Advanced or SHOPLINE will serve you better than Plus, and no Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 comparison changes that.


And if you are choosing a platform to fix an operational problem — bad inventory data, unclear channel strategy, no merchandising process — the replatform will not fix it. It will surface it, expensively, in month seven. I have watched that happen more than once, and the platform was never the variable that mattered.
